quorum_court.source: Kalawao County has no elected government. Under HRS §326-34 it is under the jurisdiction of the Hawaii Department of Health; the DOH Director is its ex-officio mayor and appoints a resident sheriff. It is the only US county with no elected governing body. 2026 legislation contemplates transferring these duties (possibly to Maui County) once no Hansen’s-disease patient-residents remain.

budget_adoption_window.note: There is no county budget; the state budget that funds the settlement is set by the Hawaii Legislature in the spring.

election_blackouts.note: Bright lines: no candidate issues, no active-ballot-measure issues, no named-individual conduct issues.

election_office.name: County of Maui, Office of the County Clerk, Elections Division
election_office.hours: Monday–Friday, 7:45 am to 4:30 pm (closed state holidays)
election_office.early_voting: State law counts Kalawao County as part of Maui County for elections, so Maui County runs voting here. Ballots come by mail by Oct. 16. On Molokai, the voter service center at Mitchell Pau'ole Center Conference Room, 90 Ainoa St., Kaunakakai, is open Oct. 31–Nov. 2 (daily except Sunday) 8 am to 4:30 pm, and 7 am to 7 pm on Nov. 3. A ballot drop box at Mitchell Pau'ole Center is open during facility hours from Oct. 14 to 7 pm on Nov. 3. The county's main center, in Wailuku, opens Oct. 20.
election_office.election_day: There are no polling places. Make sure your mail ballot arrives by 7 pm, or vote in person at a voter service center.
